selected.text: By Him Who hath raised me up, made me manifest and caused me to speak, God's love for you surpasseth that of all kindred and relatives.

selected.text: Therefore, those souls who have drunk from the choice wine of divine love and partaken of the Kawthar of recognition are in all conditions turned toward Him and holding fast to the hem of His generosity, for that which is everlasting and enduring has been and will be the love of God and His recognition.
selected.reason: Distinguishes enduring love and recognition from changing external conditions.

selected.text: Say: How many souls laid claim to love, yet were later deprived of the Lord of the Beginning and the End by a mere croak or buzz.
selected.reason: Warns against claims of love that fail under trivial opposition.

selected.text: Prefer the love of God to the love of your own selves
selected.reason: Directly contrasts love of God with self-centered attachment.

selected.text: O Isma'il! A single flame from the fire of God's love shone forth upon Solomon and set him ablaze
selected.reason: Uses Solomon as a distinct scriptural illustration of love's transforming effect.

selected.text: O handmaid of God, desire nothing from the Friend save the Friend, and seek naught from the Beloved save His good-pleasure. His favor is better than a hundred thousand children, and His good-pleasure sweeter than a hundred thousand worlds.
selected.reason: Distinguishes seeking the Beloved from seeking rewards or even paradise.

selected.text: Noble birth and exalted lineage are praiseworthy when adorned with the love of God; otherwise, if one does not attain to this most exalted station, one has not been and will never be mentioned in the presence of God.
selected.reason: Qualifies the value of social lineage by spiritual character and love.

selected.text: The beginning of the matter is the recognition of the Dawning-Place of God's Cause and the Manifestation of His Own Self, and its end is steadfastness in the love of God, exalted be His glory.
selected.reason: Connects recognition at the beginning of religious life with steadfast love at its fulfillment.

selected.text: Divine love, exalted be His glory, is like unto a precious pearl, sanctified above any likeness, similitude, peer or dwelling place, and its treasury hath ever been and shall remain the hearts.
selected.reason: Qualifies pearl imagery by asserting that love surpasses likeness and comparison.

selected.text: Be not grieved that thou hast returned to thy homeland. Though the true original home is indeed the precincts of the Throne, yet since thou didst return by God's leave and His good-pleasure, I swear by My life that it is the Kawthar of life.
selected.reason: Addresses return to one's homeland and belonging through divine good pleasure.

selected.text: They who claim to love thee, love thee only for their own sakes, whereas thy Lord loveth thee for thine own sake
selected.reason: Distinguishes self-interested affection from God's love for the person's own sake.

selected.text: His heart is a treasury of the love of God. Verily, We love him who loveth Him. That honored lady and the others should gladden him through manifestations of love and affection.
selected.reason: Asks that inward love find expression in giving another person joy and affection.

selected.text: Today kinship is not considered - thou art mentioned for the love of God
selected.reason: Distinguishes spiritual relationship from claims based on kinship.

selected.text: Then know that We loved you before as We love you now, and We mentioned you in a beautiful Tablet that you might find tranquility in your soul and be among those firm in love.
selected.reason: Gives reassurance through the continuity of divine remembrance and love.

selected.text: By Thy might, O God of the world and Desire of the nations! I love naught but what Thou lovest, and desire naught but what Thou desirest.
selected.reason: A prayer aligns the believer's desires with what God loves.

selected.text: These are the souls whose existence the denizens of the Supreme Concourse take pride in and whose presence they eagerly anticipate. Therefore strive that the Joseph of divine love not be seized by the wolves of trials.
selected.reason: Uses Joseph and the wolves to explore protecting love amid trials.

selected.text: If thou remainest firm in the love of God … for His love hath ever been and shall continue to be the teacher of pure hearts and sanctified souls
selected.reason: Describes love itself as a teacher of the heart and soul.

selected.text: your souls with courtesy, and your hearts with My love
selected.reason: Connects inward love with outward courtesy.

selected.text: We have understood the signs of thy love and the expressions of thy sincerity contained therein. We have become aware of thy state and how the fire of longing hath seized thee and how thou art consumed by the days of separation from the presence of thy Beloved, even though He is with thee at all times.
selected.reason: Distinguishes felt separation from the Beloved's continuing presence.

selected.text: "My God! my God! Thou art my hope and my beloved, my intended aim and desire! With great humbleness and entire devotion I pray to Thee"

selected.text: ...love of God, and consequently of men, is the essential foundation of every religion, our own included. A greater degree of love will produce a greater unity, because it enables people to bear with each other, to be patient and forgiving.

And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.

selected.text: I am lost, O Love, possessed and dazed, Love's fool am I, in all the earth. They call me first among the crazed, Though I once came first for wit and worth. O Love, who sellest me this wine, O Love, for whom I burn and bleed, Love, for whom I cry and pine-- Thou the Piper, I the reed. If Thou wishest me to live, Through me blow Thy holy breath. selected.original: The soul then in her natural state is in love with God and wants to be united with him... Plotinus, Enn.VI.9.9

selected.text: In loving you, what do I love? No physical beauty, no temporal glory, no radiance of light that commends itself to these eyes of mine; no sweet melody of songs tuned to every mode, no soft scent of flowers or of ointments or of perfumes, no manna, no honey, no limbs that can receive [bodily] embrace; yet I do love some kind of light, some kind of voice, some kind of fragrance, some kind of food, some kind of embrace, when I love my God, who is light, voice, fragrance, food, embrace to my inner man. There it is that a light shines on my soul that no place can contain, a sound is uttered that no time can take away, a fragrance cast that no breath of wind can disperse, a savour given forth that eating cannot blunt, and there clings to me that which cannot be torn away by satiety. This is what I love in loving my God.
selected.original: In loving you, what do I love? No physical beauty, no temporal glory, no radiance of light that commends itself to these eyes of mine; no sweet melody of songs tuned to every mode, no soft scent of flowers or of ointments or of perfumes, no manna, no honey, no limbs that can receive [bodily] embrace; yet I do love some kind of light, some kind of voice, some kind of fragrance, some kind of food, some kind of embrace, when I love my God, who is light, voice, fragrance, food, embrace to my inner man. There it is that a light shines on my soul that no place can contain, a sound is uttered that no time can take away, a fragrance cast that no breath of wind can disperse, a savour given forth that eating cannot blunt, and there clings to me that which cannot be torn away by satiety. This is what I love in loving my God. (St. Augustine, Confessions 10.6.8)
selected.reason: Augustine examines the inward meaning of the sensory language used for love of God.

authorityEvidence.authorization: Augustine quotation; supplied translator unidentified, no Bahai translation authority.
authorityEvidence.finding: Confessions X.6.8 is verified in the J.G.Pilkington edition, whose wording differs from the supplied version. Its contrast between outward sensations and inward love is present. Do not identify the supplied translator or silently replace the text.

Guard it within the globe of trust and detachment from all else but God, so that the evil whisperings of te ungodly may not extinguish its light.

selected.reference: LG#1341, UD.458 (4 Oct. 1950 on behalf of Shoghi Effendi)
selected.text: We must love God, and in this state, a general love for all men becomes possible. We cannot love each human being for himself but our feeling towards humanity should be motivated by our love for the Father who created all men.
selected.original: We must love God, and in this state, a general love for all men becomes possible. selected.reason: Explains how love for God can motivate a general love for humanity.

selected.text: Now it is evident, in accordance with what has been said, that it is love of God (caritas) which directs the acts of all other virtues to the last end and which, consequently, also gives the form to all other acts of virtue: and it is precisely in this sense that love of God (caritas) is called the form of the virtues, for these are called virtues in relation to 'informed' acts.
